ModelCharacter: Endeavour's best-selling larger power cat of the early 2000s, using an enormous 18'8" beam to deliver three staterooms, two heads, broad side decks and genuine liveaboard volume while twin Yanmar diesels provide roughly 14–15-knot cruise.
DesignLineage: Produced from 2001–2006.
The 44 expanded Endeavour's TrawlerCat formula far beyond the 36 in beam, accommodation and speed.
Galley-up and galley-down layouts were available, with most boats reportedly delivered galley-down.
Watertight collision bulkheads and recessed propellers are integral features of the catamaran hull design.
OwnershipCharacter: Extraordinary living space, but the nearly 19-foot beam strongly constrains marina, travel-lift and haul-out choices. Twin diesels and two hulls mean duplicated machinery/plumbing; access and shallow draft remain strong positives.

ModelVariations.Description: Island Gypsy models were offered in Sedan, Europa, Fisherman, Classic and motor-cruiser configurations with materially different layouts and engine packages.

ModelCharacter: The classic compact Island Gypsy sedan: a one-stateroom, single-diesel trawler with full walkaround decks, handcrafted teak interior and protected running gear. It is a direct, traditional cruising-couple boat rather than a high-volume liveaboard.
DesignLineage: Harvey Halvorsen designed the Island Gypsy range after forming the Kong & Halvorsen venture in 1975.
The 32 Sedan became one of the core sub-40-foot Island Gypsy models and was built for roughly two decades.
The 32 Europa is a later protected-deck variation of the same basic sedan-trawler concept.
The 32 Fisherman uses the same basic 32 hull mold but has a more workboat-oriented deckhouse/cockpit arrangement and different performance intent.
OwnershipCharacter: Simple and economical mechanically, especially in single-Lehman form. Teak decks, window frames, tanks and older electrical work are the main age-related ownership variables; strong construction and straightforward systems reward well-refitted examples.

ModelVariations.Name: Model-specific layouts and generations
ModelVariations.Description: Kadey-Krogen models evolved through multiple layouts and equipment packages; the 38 Cutter is a distinct sailing/motorsailing design rather than a conventional Krogen trawler.

ModelCharacter: The modern evolution of the original Krogen 42 formula: a full-displacement, transoceanic owner-operator trawler with improved structure, ergonomics and machinery access while preserving the single-engine, raised-pilothouse and deep-keel character of the earlier boat.
DesignLineage: The Krogen 44 debuted in 2004 as a refined successor to the Krogen 42.
The original 44 retained the 42's basic arrangement but gained a slightly wider beam, more pilothouse/aft-deck room and a stronger integrated pilothouse/flybridge/boat-deck structure.
The later AE designation means Advanced Ergonomics and added features such as improved engine-room access, redesigned boarding/steps and updated interior systems.
B-Atlas treats the 44 AE as the later evolutionary generation of the same Krogen 44 hull lineage, not as an unrelated model.
OwnershipCharacter: Designed specifically for an owner-operator couple and unusually serviceable for an ocean-capable yacht. It remains yacht-scale ownership, with stabilizers, generator, hydraulic systems, large tankage and substantial preventative maintenance despite the simplicity of a single main engine.

Overview: The Seaway 28 is an express cruiser and semi-displacement produced from 2008 to 2018. Typical examples use single inboard, diesel, and shaft. The recorded configuration includes 1 cabin, 4 berths, and 1 head.

ModelCharacter: A larger single-screw Downeast cruiser built for couples who want traditional workboat styling with genuinely fast coastal performance. Owner reports describe stable 20–22-knot cruising, making it a fast semi-displacement coastal cruiser rather than a conventional trawler.
DesignLineage: The 28 Coastal Cruiser belongs to Seaway's recreational Downeast line and is distinct from the smaller 24 Sport Trawler.
The hull retains single-screw workboat-derived architecture while carrying more cruising accommodation and speed.
Owner experience consistently identifies roughly 20–22-knot normal cruise with suitable power.
Because primary factory documentation is sparse, B-Atlas preserves production chronology and exact standard specifications as unknown where not independently verified.
OwnershipCharacter: Single-engine machinery is simpler than twin-engine express cruisers, but prop walk and low-speed handling can be challenging; owners specifically note the benefit of a bow thruster. Survey should focus on running gear, steering, core, tanks and drivetrain alignment.

TypicalMission: Family coastal cruising and light sportfishing

ModelCharacter: A classic 1970s Universal Marine Europa trawler with a single Ford Lehman diesel, long covered side decks and a teak-rich interior, combining the practical weather protection of a sedan/Europa layout with slow, economical shaft-drive cruising.
DesignLineage: Verified 1977 Universal Marine Europa examples establish a distinct approximately 40-foot model.
Period and surviving records also use Pacific 38/Pacific 40 or generic Universal Trawler wording, illustrating inconsistent distributor naming rather than necessarily different hulls.
The Europa's long covered side decks and sedan-oriented superstructure distinguish it from Universal's tri-cabin 36.
Because factory documentation is scarce, B-Atlas uses Universal Marine 40 Europa as the canonical searchable identity while retaining Pacific/Universal Trawler names as aliases.
OwnershipCharacter: Single-Lehman operation is economical and mechanically simple, but a 40-foot teak-decked Taiwan trawler carries substantial restoration exposure. Deck moisture, windows, steel fuel tanks, wiring and prior structural repairs matter more than the low-powered drivetrain.
